questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: A left arm extended upward means the driver is turning right. Adjust your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under dangerous conditions.
The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed to travel on a road under ideal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions. You can drive slower than the limit, but not faster. Slow down for school zones, work zones, and bad weather or construction.

questions.question: Which is not a factor in determining the distance needed to stop your vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on speed and road conditions.

questions.question: A "No stopping" sign means you may stop only if:

options.text: To avoid conflict with other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid conflict with other traffic.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, follow a police officer's direction, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: When parking uphill on an incline with a curb:

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parked uphill. This stops your vehicle from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time, which must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: At any intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle has no Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Firmly pump your brakes.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop in an emergency. Your car stops quickly and you can still steer.

questions.question: When you see a steady green arrow, you:

options.text: Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Should slow down and stop if safe.
May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
May drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane and yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves right and then left. Slow down to safely navigate these curves.

questions.question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, a driver should:

options.text: Stop at the intersection, check in all directions, and proceed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to yield.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be ready to yield by taking your foot off the gas, covering the brake, and looking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on open mountain highways when no sign says otherwise?
questions.correctAnswerText: 40 mph
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit on open mountain highways is 40 mph unless a sign shows a different speed. Always follow posted speed limit signs.

questions.question: You are driving in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders for other vehicles before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and turn on your signal. Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane early. Slow down only after you are in the exit lane. Do not slow down before you move into it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: A driver's left arm and hand extended downward means they are stopping. Adjust your driving if you are following this vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycles is true?

options.text: It is okay for drivers of other vehicles to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two people on it is more balanced than a motorcycle with just one rider.
The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.
Drivers of other vehicles can expect a motorcycle's brake lights to turn on when the motorcyclist slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need a full lane of space. Move your entire vehicle into the left lane before passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow at a traffic signal, what should you do?

options.text: Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.
May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way and may expect oncoming traffic to stop for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop safely unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing with no traffic signals?

options.text: Always bring the car to a complete stop.
Slow down and be prepared to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals so you will never encounter this situation.
Increase your speed to get across the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down at unmarked railroad crossings. Look and listen for trains coming from both directions. Only cross when you are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: How are reversible lanes marked?
questions.correctAnswerText: Double broken yellow lines.
questions.explanation: Reversible lanes carry traffic in one direction at certain times and the opposite direction at other times. They are marked with double broken yellow lines or separated by a barrier.

questions.question: When does your vehicle need more distance to stop?

options.text: On a wet or icy road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Wet and icy roads increase your stopping distance. Loose gravel and stone also increase stopping distance.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show directions and distances to drivers.
questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background. They show directions and distances to specific places. They help drivers who are not familiar with the area.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and as fast as you can.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains before crossing railroad tracks. Do not cross until your whole vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing because your vehicle could stall.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic lanes moving in opposite directions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions on the road.

questions.question: When a traffic light changes from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, you should:

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless stopping would be unsafe.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless stopping would be unsafe.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow light, slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: You should be careful when passing a bicycle because:

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.
questions.explanation: A cyclist may have to swerve suddenly into traffic to avoid an object on the road. Always drive carefully around bicyclists.
